characters.name: Hal Jordan
characters.tagline: The Corps' greatest — and most reckless — Lantern.
characters.bio: Hal Jordan was a fearless test pilot for Ferris Aircraft when the dying alien Abin Sur passed him a power ring — and the Guardians' choice proved inspired, if endlessly exasperating. Where other Lanterns recite procedure, Hal improvises: he has punched through armies, outflown supernovae, and talked his way out of cosmic courts, all on the strength of a willpower so absolute it borders on defiance of reality itself. Trained by Sinestro himself, Hal inherited his mentor's brilliance and rejected his mentor's tyranny — a tension that has defined both men ever since. His fall was the Corps' darkest hour: when Coast City was destroyed, Hal's grief broke him, and as Parallax he unmade the Corps itself in Emerald Twilight. But Green Lantern: Rebirth revealed the truth — a fear entity had been festering in his ring all along — and Hal's return rebuilt the mythology from the foundation up. He went on to lead the Corps through the Sinestro Corps War, Blackest Night, and the War of the Green Lanterns, forging the rainbow coalition that saved the universe. Whether as the Corps' greatest hero, its prodigal exile, or Morrison's intergalactic lawman, Hal Jordan remains the standard every Lantern is measured against: the man with the will to do anything, and the recklessness to try. He has died, been reborn, wielded every color of the spectrum, and faced down gods — yet his defining trait never changed: when everyone else sees the odds, Hal sees the opening. That is why the ring chose him, why it keeps choosing him, and why the Corps' oath might as well have been written about one man.
characters.signature: Giant boxing-glove construct — the most famous hard-light creation in comics.

characters.name: John Stewart
characters.bio: John Stewart is an architect and former U.S. Marine, chosen for a mind like a precision instrument. Where Hal Jordan improvises, John plans three moves ahead — the Corps' strategist and its moral center. His constructs are famous for their detail: John doesn't just imagine a wall, he imagines every brick. He carries the weight of Xanshi, a world he once failed to save, and it made him the most careful Lantern alive.
characters.signature: Architectural constructs built with engineer's precision; once sniped a target from 3 sectors away.

characters.name: Guy Gardner
characters.bio: Guy Gardner is the Corps' brawler — loud, proud, and utterly fearless, with a chip on his shoulder the size of Oa. Beneath the bluster is one of the most loyal Lanterns alive; Guy has bled for the Corps more times than he'll admit. He's worn many rings in his time — green, red, even the mantle of a Warrior — and led the Green Lantern Corps Honor Guard. All attitude on the surface, all heart underneath.
characters.signature: A giant green fist — subtle as a brick, twice as effective.

characters.name: Kyle Rayner
characters.tagline: The artist who became the White Lantern.
characters.bio: Kyle Rayner was a freelance artist handed a power ring on the worst day of the Corps' history — with almost no training and no Corps to train him. Where Hal Jordan was a test pilot who imposed his will on the universe, Kyle was an illustrator who imagined his way through it: his constructs had an artist's flair, detailed and inventive in ways no Lantern before him had attempted. Thrust into the role during Emerald Twilight's aftermath, Kyle carried the entire Green Lantern legacy alone through the late 1990s, earning the name Torchbearer. He briefly wielded the godlike power of Ion, sacrificed it to reignite the Central Power Battery and resurrect the Guardians, and stood at Hal's side through the Sinestro Corps War and Blackest Night. His greatest feat came later: journeying across the emotional spectrum in Green Lantern: New Guardians, Kyle mastered all seven lights and became the White Lantern — the living embodiment of life itself. The kid who got the last ring became the one Lantern who could wield them all. Unlike Hal, Kyle never had a mentor's shadow to escape — he had a vacuum to fill, and he filled it with imagination. His era proved the Corps was an idea bigger than any one bearer, and his White Lantern ascension proved that the idea's fullest expression belonged to the artist who never stopped drawing new possibilities. When the history of the Corps is written, Kyle's chapter is the one about reinvention.
characters.signature: Intricate, artistic constructs — he thinks in illustrations, not weapons.

characters.name: Kilowog
characters.bio: Kilowog is a towering Bolovaxian who has served as the Green Lantern Corps' drill sergeant for generations. Every rookie's first day runs through him — and nobody forgets it. He lost his entire homeworld when Bolovax Vik was destroyed, and carries his people in his heart into every battle. Gruff, profane, and fiercely loyal: the backbone of the Corps.
characters.signature: A massive power hammer; also the Corps' drill sergeant — "poozers" beware.

characters.name: Sinestro
characters.tagline: The Corps' greatest enemy — and its greatest cautionary tale.
characters.bio: Thaal Sinestro was once the Green Lantern Corps' most celebrated member — the greatest Lantern of his era, and Hal Jordan's own mentor. A Korugarian anthropologist obsessed with order, Sinestro decided that his homeworld's peace required his absolute rule, and he built a dictatorship with his power ring, crushing dissent in the name of stability. When Hal exposed him, the Guardians stripped Sinestro of his ring and exiled him to the antimatter universe of Qward — where he did what exiles do: he built an army. Forging the yellow ring from the fear entity Parallax, Sinestro founded the Sinestro Corps on a single doctrine: where the Guardians offer willpower, he offers the order that only terror can enforce. He has died and returned, conquered and been conquered, led his Corps in the war that bears his name and stood beside Hal against the Black Lanterns. In the New 52 he even wore green again, however briefly, and his solo series asked the uncomfortable question: can fear serve justice? Sinestro endures because he is never merely a villain — he is the Corps' mirror, the argument that willpower without order is chaos, made by the one man brilliant enough to almost prove it. His relationship with his daughter Soranik Natu — a Green Lantern herself — adds the one complication his philosophy cannot resolve: love. Every era of Green Lantern reinvents Sinestro, because every era needs to ask his question again: how much order is worth how much freedom?
characters.signature: Fear made manifest — his constructs don't just hurt you, they terrify you first.

characters.name: Arkillo
characters.bio: Arkillo is a savage warrior of the planet Vorn, recruited for his singular gift: inspiring terror. He serves the Sinestro Corps as its brutal drill sergeant — the yellow answer to Kilowog. All muscle, all menace, all fear: the Corps' enforcer and Sinestro's most loyal hound.
characters.signature: Brute-force yellow constructs; famously had his ring finger bitten off by Kilowog.

characters.name: Atrocitus
characters.tagline: Founder of the Red Lanterns — rage with a prophecy.
characters.bio: Atrocitus — born Atros on the planet Ryut in Sector 666 — is one of the Five Inversions, the only survivors of the Manhunters' massacre of his sector. For centuries, the Inversions waged a blood-magic war on the Guardians, building the Empire of Tears from their prison on Ysmault. But Atros had gazed into his own future using a murdered Guardian's blood: he saw himself standing over his comrades' corpses. He made it real — bludgeoning Qull to death with the first red power battery, then bleeding out Roixeaume, Orphram, and Dal Xauix. Their crystallized blood became the first red ring; their sacrifice raised the Red Central Power Battery over Ysmault's lake of blood. As the first Red Lantern, Atrocitus doesn't just burn — he burns with purpose: vengeance on the Guardians, war on Sinestro, and a prophecy of the Blackest Night that drove him to forge an army from rage itself.
characters.signature: Rage plasma — his ring replaces the heart and lets him vomit corrosive blood-fire.

characters.name: Bleez
characters.tagline: Winged fury of the Red Lanterns.
characters.bio: Bleez was a princess of Havania, whose beauty was matched only by the fury the Sinestro Corps' invasion lit in her. The red ring found her drowning in rage — and made her one of the Red Lanterns' most formidable warriors. Of all the Corps' berserkers, she kept the most of her mind: fury with a focus. Her rage is as beautiful as it is terrible.
characters.firstAppearance: Final Crisis: Rage of the Red Lanterns #1 (2008)
characters.signature: Razor-edged rage constructs; her wings are living weapons.

characters.name: Dex-Starr
characters.bio: Dex-Starr was an ordinary housecat, abandoned and abused, until rage at a cruel world earned him a red ring. Do not let the cuteness fool you: he is small, adorable, and utterly lethal — the Red Lanterns' mascot and one of their deadliest weapons. The most dangerous kitty in the universe.
characters.firstAppearance: Final Crisis: Rage of the Red Lanterns #1 (2008)
characters.signature: The rage kitten — small, blue, and utterly murderous.

characters.name: Zilius Zox
characters.bio: Zilius Zox is a hulking brute of the same species as the fallen Green Lantern Galius Zed. Where Atrocitus schemes and Bleez seethes, Zox simply rages — rage in its purest, simplest form. All muscle, all fury: the Red Lanterns' bluntest instrument.
characters.firstAppearance: Final Crisis: Rage of the Red Lanterns #1 (2008)
characters.signature: Acidic bile constructs — disgusting and devastating.

characters.name: Rankorr
characters.bio: Jack Moore was an ordinary young man until grief and fury earned him a red ring — and he became Rankorr. Unlike most Red Lanterns, something human survived in him: he fights the rage from the inside, every day. The most human heart in the most inhuman Corps.
characters.signature: Chains and blades forged from pure rage.

characters.name: Skallox
characters.bio: Skallox was once an interrogator for a crime syndicate — until his own boss betrayed him and threw him into a furnace. He crawled out with his rage intact, and the red ring found him. Now he serves as the Red Lantern Corps' enforcer, the one Atrocitus sends when the message needs to be unmistakable.
characters.firstAppearance: Final Crisis: Rage of the Red Lanterns #1 (2008)
characters.signature: Skull-faced intimidation constructs.

characters.name: Vice
characters.bio: Vice is the most ruthless hunter of the Red Lantern Corps — a pincer-jawed predator with no mercy and no off switch. His mate was devoured by Arkillo of the Sinestro Corps, and his rage has never cooled since. The thing Red Lanterns point at other Red Lanterns.
characters.firstAppearance: Final Crisis: Rage of the Red Lanterns #1 (2008)
characters.signature: Brutal close-combat rage weapons.

characters.name: Laira
characters.tagline: Honor Guard discipline, Red Lantern rage.
characters.bio: Laira Omoto was an honored Green Lantern of Sector 112, a member of the elite Honor Guard — the Corps' most disciplined soldier. But in a moment of rage she crossed a line no Lantern should cross, and a red ring found her in the aftermath. Honor Guard training, Red Lantern fury: one of the most dangerous warriors in either Corps.
characters.signature: A warrior's arsenal — she was a Green Lantern before rage took her.

characters.name: Larfleeze
characters.bio: Larfleeze is a miserable wretch who found the orange light of avarice and claimed it — all of it, forever. He is the entire Orange Lantern Corps: one being, one ring, infinite greed. The identities of everyone he has consumed live on as his constructs, an army of the stolen. He wants it ALL, and he is not sharing.
characters.firstAppearance: Green Lantern (vol. 4) #25 (2008) — cameo; first full appearance in #39 (2009)
characters.signature: His entire corps is one construct army — the stolen identities of everyone he's killed.

characters.name: Glomulus
characters.bio: Glomulus was a tavern pest on Okaara with a taste for blood — he ate the whole bar. Larfleeze consumed him for it, and now the little glutton serves as one of the Orange Lantern's most loyal constructs. Proof that in the Orange Corps, even being eaten is just a career change.
characters.signature: A construct sidekick with a heart (sort of).

characters.name: Saint Walker
characters.bio: Saint Walker was a gentle soul on the dying world of Astonia when the blue light of hope chose him as the first Blue Lantern. Where others preach hope, he simply is it — quiet, kind, and unbreakable. His first great act was reigniting his own dying sun. Hope's gentlest warrior, and its most convincing.
characters.firstAppearance: Final Crisis: Rage of the Red Lanterns #1 (2008)
characters.signature: Hope constructs that heal — his light once reignited a dying sun.

characters.name: Brother Warth
characters.bio: Brother Warth is a calm, elephantine alien chosen by Saint Walker as one of the very first Blue Lanterns. Gentle in manner and unshakable in hope, he stood beside Saint Walker for the Blue Corps' first great feat: reigniting a dying sun. Hope's gentle giant.
characters.signature: Gentle hope constructs; an elephantine optimist.

characters.name: Sister Sercy
characters.bio: Sister Sercy was the fourth to join the Blue Lantern Corps, chosen to carry hope back to her sector. She sought the blue light to free her homeworld from the tyrant Evil Star — a mission of hope against impossible odds. Hope for her homeworld — and everyone else's.
characters.signature: Hope given sharp edges.

characters.name: Indigo-1
characters.bio: Indigo-1 is the enigmatic bearer of the indigo staff, leading a tribe that wields compassion itself as a weapon. Her past is a mystery the light keeps — and the Tribe keeps its secrets. What is known: where she walks, the merciless learn mercy, channeled through her staff.
characters.signature: Her staff channels any light — she's wielded them all.

characters.name: Munk
characters.bio: Munk is the second-in-command of the Indigo Tribe and Indigo-1's most trusted. A towering, silent presence who channels the indigo light of compassion through his staff. Where Indigo-1 leads, Munk enforces — with mercy, whether the target wants it or not.
characters.signature: Compassion constructs that bind rather than break.

characters.name: Carol Ferris
characters.bio: Carol Ferris is the heiress of Ferris Aircraft and Hal Jordan's great love — chosen by the violet light of love as the queen of the Star Sapphires. Torn between her heart and her duty, between Hal and her Corps, she has fought for love on every side of every war. A queen caught in the middle of everything.
characters.signature: Crystal-heart constructs — love as a weapon and a shield.

characters.name: Fatality
characters.bio: Yrra Cynril was the princess of Xanshi — the same world whose death haunts John Stewart. She hunted Lanterns across the stars as Fatality, blaming the Corps for her world's fate, until the violet light of love claimed the hunter herself. Love, at last, gave her something to protect instead of something to avenge.
characters.signature: A violet energy arsenal aimed at one target: Sinestro.

characters.name: Queen Aga'po
characters.bio: Queen Aga'po rules the Zamarons and the Star Sapphire Corps she built — forging the violet light of love into rings and a Central Power Battery. She is determined to spread love across the universe. By force, if needed: the Zamarons' love has always come with sharp edges.
characters.signature: Royal violet constructs of overwhelming force.

characters.name: Black Hand
characters.bio: William Hand has been obsessed with death since childhood — a lifelong Green Lantern foe who found his calling as the herald of the Black Lantern Corps. Where he points, the dead rise, and he preaches death's gospel with a convert's zeal. Death's favorite hand, and its loudest prophet.
characters.signature: Death constructs — he wields the black ring that started it all.

characters.name: Nekron
characters.bio: Nekron is death given will and voice — the Lord of the Unliving, and the power behind the Blackest Night itself. He is the darkness every light in the universe was made to hold back, and his black rings raise the dead to snuff out all emotion. When the dead rise, he is why.
characters.firstAppearance: Tales of the Green Lantern Corps #2 (1981)
characters.signature: The Lord of the Unliving doesn't need constructs. He has your corpse.

characters.name: Scar
characters.bio: Scar was a Guardian of the Universe — until the Anti-Monitor's touch scarred her during the Sinestro Corps War. The wound never healed, and something dark took root in the scar. Now she stands among the Black Lanterns: a Guardian, unmade, and the crack through which the darkness entered.
characters.signature: A Guardian's power turned to death's service.

characters.name: Lyssa Drak
characters.bio: A Talokite woman who serves as the Keeper of the Book of Parallax, the Sinestro Corps' dark counterpart to the Guardians' Book of Oa, which she carries chained to her wrist. Cold, scholarly, and utterly devoted to Sinestro's vision, she fancies herself the historian of fear itself — she famously boasts that she knows fear "like no other." Captured by the Green Lantern Corps during the Sinestro Corps War and imprisoned in a Sciencell on Oa, she later escaped to continue chronicling the Corps' conquests. Her knowledge of the Corps' prophecies makes her one of its most dangerous non-combatants. She remains Sinestro's most loyal scribe, recording every atrocity as though it were scripture.
characters.signature: The Book of Parallax — she doesn't fight, she records your doom.

characters.name: Karu-Sil
characters.tagline: Raised by beasts; feared by all.
characters.bio: A native of Graxos III — the same world as the Green Lantern Arisia Rrab — Karu-Sil was the sole survivor of a raid that wiped out her village as a child, and was raised by a pack of wild beasts. To bond with her new family she carved her own mouth into a permanent rictus grin mirroring theirs, and she never left the wild behind. A yellow power ring chose her for her capacity to instill great fear, and she fights alongside hard-light constructs of her beloved animal pack. Feral, fiercely loyal, and utterly without mercy, she is one of the Sinestro Corps' most savage enforcers. Her tragedy is that the pack she loves exists now only as ring-light.
characters.signature: Feral fear constructs; raised by monsters, fights like one.

characters.name: Despotellis
characters.bio: Despotellis is a sentient bio-virus and one of the most insidious living weapons ever recruited into the Sinestro Corps. Microscopic and virtually undetectable, he kills from inside his victims' bodies, spreading plague and terror that no shield can keep out. Sinestro deployed him as a weapon of mass destruction during the Sinestro Corps War, and Despotellis has wiped out entire planetary populations on his own. He embodies fear at its most intimate — the terror of an enemy already inside you. Even among the fear-wielding Corps, he is regarded with horror.
characters.signature: A sentient virus — fear you can't punch.

characters.name: Tomar-Re
characters.bio: A Xudarian — a proud, bird-like alien — Tomar-Re was one of the Green Lantern Corps' most respected veterans, serving as the Lantern of Sector 2813 for decades. A scientist and diplomat by temperament, he was a close friend of Abin Sur and later a mentor figure to Earth's Lanterns, including Hal Jordan. His defining sorrow is that he once flew to save the planet Krypton but arrived too late — a failure that haunted him for the rest of his life. Wise, compassionate, and scholarly, he represented the Corps' ideals at their best. His son Tomar-Tu would later follow him into the Corps, carrying on the family legacy.
characters.signature: A scholar's precise, efficient constructs.

characters.name: Salaak
characters.tagline: Keeper of the Book of Oa.
characters.bio: A four-armed, pink-skinned alien, Salaak is one of the Corps' longest-serving members and its resident pessimist — the Lantern most likely to point out everything that could go wrong. Beneath the gloom beats a deeply loyal heart: he rose to become the Corps' chief administrator on Oa, keeper of the Book of Oa and drillmaster to generations of recruits. By-the-book and protocol-obsessed, he clashed often with mavericks like Guy Gardner, yet his discipline held the Corps together through its darkest hours. His dour exterior hides a profound devotion to the Green Lantern ideal. When the Corps needs order, it turns to Salaak.
characters.signature: Protocol-perfect constructs; the Corps' rulebook made light.

characters.name: Arisia Rrab
characters.firstAppearance: Tales of the Green Lantern Corps #1 (1981)
characters.bio: A Graxosian recruited into the Corps at just thirteen years old, Arisia used her power ring to age herself into adulthood so she could serve — a choice that defined her fierce determination to be taken seriously. Gold-skinned and white-haired, she became one of the Corps' most earnest young Lanterns and famously shared a romance with Hal Jordan. She endured the Crisis on Infinite Earths, which unmade and remade her world and her life, yet she always returned to the uniform. Brave, idealistic, and eager to prove herself, Arisia embodies the Corps' promise that willpower matters more than age. She remains one of its most beloved veterans.
characters.signature: Youthful, creative constructs — she joined the Corps as a teenager.

characters.name: Soranik Natu
characters.bio: A brilliant neurosurgeon from Korugar — Sinestro's homeworld, where Green Lanterns were despised — Soranik initially refused her power ring, accepting it only to save a dying patient on the operating table. She quickly proved one of the finest Lanterns of her generation: disciplined, compassionate, and utterly fearless in the field. Her life was upended by the revelation that she is Sinestro's own daughter, a legacy she has spent years both rejecting and reckoning with. She shared a deep bond with Kyle Rayner, who saw past her father's shadow to the hero she chose to become. A healer first and a warrior second, Soranik fights to redeem both her world and her bloodline.
characters.signature: A surgeon's precision — she was a doctor before she was a Lantern.

characters.name: Ganthet
characters.bio: Ganthet is a Guardian of the Universe — but unlike his cold, detached brethren, he never lost his capacity to feel. He befriended Kyle Rayner when the Corps was at its lowest, defied the other Guardians to protect Earth's Lanterns, and always believed emotion was a strength rather than a flaw. After the Sinestro Corps War, he and Sayd were banished from Oa for embracing feeling — so together they founded the Blue Lantern Corps on the planet Odym, wielding the blue light of hope. As the Blue Lanterns' leader, he became living proof that hope can move even the oldest and most rigid of beings. Warm, wise, and quietly rebellious, Ganthet is the Guardian with a heart.
characters.signature: A Guardian's will — small in stature, immeasurable in power.

characters.name: Sayd
characters.bio: Sayd is a Guardian of the Universe and Ganthet's closest confidante — together they were the only Guardians who showed compassion when the Sinestro Corps War demanded it. Where the other Guardians saw emotion as weakness, Sayd saw it as truth, and she stood by Ganthet when that belief got them both exiled from Oa. On the planet Odym she co-founded the Blue Lantern Corps, becoming one of the first wielders of the blue light of hope. Gentle, empathetic, and quietly resolute, she is the Corps' spiritual anchor. Her hope is not naive optimism but a deliberate, defiant choice — and it has never wavered.
characters.signature: Hope's co-founder; her constructs carry the dawn.

characters.name: Brother Hynn
characters.bio: Brother Hynn is an amphibious, fish-like alien and one of the earliest recruits of the Blue Lantern Corps, drawn to Odym by the promise of hope. A devout and humble soul, he serves the Corps faithfully from their homeworld, standing alongside Saint Walker, Brother Warth, and Sister Sercy as hope's quiet foot soldiers. Though a minor figure in the Corps' history, his steadfast faith embodies what the blue light is all about — ordinary beings choosing hope in a dark universe. He remains a loyal Blue Lantern to this day.
characters.signature: Quiet, steadfast hope constructs.

characters.name: Miri Riam
characters.bio: Miri Riam of the planet Lartnec was a young newlywed whose honeymoon was shattered when the ravenous Mongul destroyed her ship and killed her husband Kered. Adrift in space and drowning in grief, she was on the verge of taking her own life when a violet Star Sapphire ring found her — drawn to the enormity of the love in her heart — making her the first new recruit of the reformed Star Sapphire Corps. Trained on Zamaron under Queen Aga'po, she learned to turn her great love into great strength. She later proved herself pursuing the child-stealing Sinestro Corps member Kryb across the stars. Fierce, loving, and unbreakable, Miri shows that love, wielded with conviction, is one of the universe's mightiest forces.
characters.signature: Love constructs tinged with grief — she lost everything to rage.

characters.name: Sodam Yat
characters.bio: Sodam Yat is a Daxamite — a member of the same super-powered alien race as Mon-El — who became the Green Lantern of Sector 1760. As a boy on the isolationist world of Daxam, he dreamed of the stars despite his parents' xenophobic teachings, and Alan Moore's classic "Tygers" prophecy named him the Corps' ultimate future Lantern. Under a yellow sun, Daxamites possess Superman-level strength, speed, and invulnerability — stacked on top of a power ring, that made Yat one of the most formidable Lanterns alive. During the Sinestro Corps War he became the host of Ion, the living embodiment of willpower, wielding godlike power against the forces of fear. His story is one of prophecy fulfilled: the sheltered boy who became the Corps' greatest weapon.
characters.firstAppearance: Tales of the Green Lantern Corps Annual #2 (1986)
characters.signature: As Ion's host, his constructs were godlike — willpower incarnate.

characters.name: Katma Tui
characters.tagline: The first female Green Lantern — John's mentor and wife.
characters.bio: Katma Tui was the Green Lantern of Sector 1417 and the first female Green Lantern ever introduced in the comics. A native of Korugar — the same world as Sinestro — she took over the sector after his fall and proved herself one of the Corps' finest. She later became John Stewart's mentor, training Earth's newest Lantern, and the two fell in love and married. Her murder at the hands of Star Sapphire remains one of the most infamous tragedies in Green Lantern history. Known to her people as "Katma Tui the Lost," she is remembered as a pioneer who opened the Corps to a new generation.
characters.signature: A pioneer's constructs — the first woman to wield the green light.

characters.name: Ch'p
characters.bio: Ch'p is a squirrel-like alien from the planet H'lven and the Green Lantern of Sector 1014 — and one of the most beloved oddballs in the Corps. Captured and sentenced to death by the invading Doctor Ub'x, he was offered a power ring by a Guardian in his cell and used it to liberate his homeworld. Trained by Kilowog alongside Hal Jordan's class, he became a trusted and capable Lantern despite his diminutive size. He later settled on Earth with the Corps' Earth contingent, where his small stature made him a master of stealth missions. Ch'p proves the ring chooses the worthy, whatever their shape.
characters.signature: Tiny, clever constructs — proof size doesn't matter to a ring.

characters.name: Galius Zed
characters.first: Tales of the Green Lantern Corps #2 (1981)
characters.bio: The Green Lantern with the giant head — literally. Galius Zed is a Noc'sagian, a race whose bodies are essentially one enormous cranium with arms and legs extending directly from it, built to survive their homeworld's crushing gravity. Quick-tempered, outspoken, and always first to volunteer for a fight, Zed served as a foil to Hal Jordan and even rebelled against the Guardians when he learned they'd withheld yellow-immune rings. Murdered by Fatality during her vendetta against the Corps, he later rose as a Black Lantern. His unforgettable design made him a fan favorite across comics, animation, and the 2011 film.
characters.firstAppearance: Tales of the Green Lantern Corps #2 (1981)

characters.name: Jessica Cruz
characters.first: Green Lantern #20 (2013) — cameo; full debut Justice League (vol. 2) #31 (2014)
characters.bio: The first female human Green Lantern — and one of the most human heroes in the Corps. Jessica Cruz, a Mexican-American from Portland, didn't seek out heroism: a cursed ring from another universe forced itself onto her, and she spent her early days fighting crippling anxiety as much as supervillains. What makes her extraordinary is that she won anyway — mastering her fear through sheer willpower until a true Green Lantern ring chose her on merit. Now a mainstay of both the Corps and the Justice League, she partners with Simon Baz as Earth's newest generation of Lanterns, proving that courage isn't the absence of fear but what you do with it.
characters.firstAppearance: Green Lantern #20 (2013) — cameo; first full appearance in Justice League (vol. 2) #31 (2014)

characters.name: Simon Baz
characters.first: The New 52 Free Comic Book Day Special Edition #1 (2012) — cameo; proper debut Green Lantern #0 (2012)
characters.bio: The first Muslim-American Green Lantern, and the Corps' most unlikely recruit. Simon Baz, a Lebanese-American mechanic from Dearborn, Michigan, was chosen by a ring in the chaos after Hal Jordan's apparent death — a working-class kid suddenly handed the universe's most powerful weapon. His early days were defined by distrust: of the authorities hunting him, and of the ring itself, which is why he famously carries a sidearm as backup. But Simon's stubborn decency won out, earning him a place in the Justice League and a partnership with Jessica Cruz. He represents a Green Lantern for the modern age — flawed, grounded, and utterly determined.
characters.firstAppearance: The New 52 Free Comic Book Day Special Edition #1 (2012) — cameo; debut in Green Lantern #0 (2012)

characters.name: Abin Sur
characters.tagline: The Lantern whose death made Hal Jordan.
characters.bio: Abin Sur was the Green Lantern of Sector 2814 — the sector containing Earth — long before Hal Jordan ever touched a ring. A history professor from the planet Ungara, he served the Corps with distinction until his ship was damaged by yellow radiation and he crash-landed in the California desert. Dying, he commanded his ring to find a worthy successor. It chose test pilot Hal Jordan, and the modern Green Lantern era began. Abin Sur's legacy echoes through every story that follows: his capture of Atrocitus, his discovery of the Blackest Night prophecy, and his mentorship of a young Sinestro all shaped the universe Hal inherited.
characters.signature: His dying command — 'find a worthy successor' — chose Hal Jordan and launched the Silver Age of Green Lantern.

characters.name: Mogo
characters.tagline: The living planet. Mogo doesn't socialize.
characters.bio: Mogo is a sentient planet and a full member of the Green Lantern Corps — one of its most powerful. Created by Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons in the legendary six-page story 'Mogo Doesn't Socialize,' he guides the Corps' rings to their bearers and serves as a sanctuary for Lanterns to recover. His sheer scale makes him a force unlike any other Lantern: when the Sinestro Corps came for the Green Lanterns, they came for Mogo too. A living world wearing the green light, Mogo is proof that willpower takes every shape imaginable.
characters.signature: A planet-sized Lantern whose foliage forms the Corps symbol — 'Mogo doesn't socialize.'

characters.name: Boodikka
characters.tagline: The Bellatrix warrior. First of the Alpha Lanterns.
characters.bio: Boodikka of Bellatrix was a mercenary with the Bellatrix Bombers before the Corps recruited her — a warrior who joined because she believed a Green Lantern could never be defeated. She proved herself one of the Corps' fiercest fighters, standing against Hal Jordan during Emerald Twilight and surviving what most did not. After the Sinestro Corps War, she became a charter member of the Alpha Lanterns, the Corps' internal affairs division, her body enhanced with Manhunter technology. Her arc — from mercenary to the Corps' conscience — is one of its most compelling.
characters.signature: Charter Alpha Lantern — the Corps policing itself, at the cost of her own humanity.

characters.name: Isamot Kol
characters.tagline: Saved from execution by a ring.
characters.bio: Isamot Kol is a Lizarkon — a reptilian humanoid from Thanagar — who was about to be executed for killing his commanding officer when a Green Lantern ring stopped the axe mid-swing. Recruited in Green Lantern Corps: Recharge alongside his partner Vath Sarn, Kol brought a soldier's discipline and a fierce moral code to the rebuilt Corps. Named for editor Peter Tomasi (spelled backward), he became one of the most dependable Lanterns of the modern era, serving through the Sinestro Corps War and beyond.
characters.signature: A ring interrupted his execution — and made him one of the Corps' most loyal soldiers.

characters.name: B'dg
characters.tagline: Ch'p's successor — the squirrel Lantern of Sector 1014.
characters.bio: B'dg is a squirrel-like alien from the planet H'lven, chosen to succeed the legendary Ch'p as Green Lantern of Sector 1014. Created by Geoff Johns and Ethan Van Sciver, B'dg brings the same fearless heart as his predecessor — proving that heroism comes in all sizes. He later joined the Blue Lantern Corps as well.
characters.signature: Smallest Lantern, biggest heart

characters.name: Rot Lop Fan
characters.tagline: The blind Lantern — the F-Sharp Bell.
characters.bio: Rot Lop Fan hails from the Obsidian Deeps, a lightless region where his species evolved without sight. Recruited by Katma Tui, he couldn't comprehend 'green' or 'lantern' — so she reimagined his ring as the F-Sharp Bell, wielding sound instead of light. Created by Alan Moore and Bill Willingham, he's one of the Corps' most unique members.
characters.firstAppearance: Tales of the Green Lantern Corps Annual #3 (1987)
characters.signature: In loudest din or hush profound...

characters.name: Stel
characters.tagline: The robot Lantern — 60 tons of willpower.
characters.bio: Stel is a sentient robot from the planet Grenda, where all life is mechanical. One of the earliest alien Lanterns (debuting in 1962), Stel was trained by Sinestro himself before the Korugarian's fall. Weighing 60 tons and standing 8'6", Stel computes the odds of success on every mission — then tries to beat them. He was torn apart by Krona and rebuilt, served through Crisis on Infinite Earths, and became the Corps' drill instructor after Kilowog stepped down.
characters.signature: Reckless for a robot

characters.name: Medphyll
characters.tagline: The plant Lantern — mind-stalks and photosynthesis.
characters.bio: Medphyll is a sentient plant from the world J586, where flora is the dominant life form. With bark-like skin, root-feet, and photosynthetic 'mind stalks' instead of hair, Medphyll can transfer his consciousness into any nearby plant life — making him the Corps' ultimate reconnaissance agent. He famously aided Swamp Thing in Alan Moore's run (Swamp Thing vol. 2 #61, 1987) and served with distinction through the Crisis on Infinite Earths.
characters.signature: The Corps' botanist

characters.name: Amon Sur
characters.tagline: Abin Sur's son — the Sinestro Corps' heir of resentment.
characters.bio: Amon Sur is the son of Abin Sur, the Green Lantern whose death passed the ring to Hal Jordan. Feeling abandoned by a father who chose the Corps over family, Amon became leader of the Black Circle crime syndicate, nursing a hatred for all Green Lanterns. He was recruited into the Sinestro Corps during the Sinestro Corps War, wielding a yellow ring fueled by his rage and jealousy. His story ended at the hands of Laira, the Green Lantern who executed him for his crimes. He was later resurrected as a Black Lantern during Blackest Night, turning his resentment into undeath.
characters.signature: A yellow ring turned against the Corps his father served — resentment made manifest.
characters.sources: Judd Winick, Ben Raab (writers), Charlie Adlard (artist)

characters.name: Vath Sarn
characters.tagline: Rannian soldier — from the Rann-Thanagar War to the Corps.
characters.bio: Vath Sarn was a soldier in the Rannian army during the brutal Rann-Thanagar War when a Green Lantern ring chose him mid-battle. He tried to use it to kill his Thanagarian enemies, but the ring's prohibition on lethal force would only let him destroy their weapons. Paired with Isamot Kol — a Thanagarian who had fought against him — Vath became a symbol of the Corps' power to unite ancient enemies. He served through the Sinestro Corps War and Blackest Night, evolving from a prejudiced grunt into a respected Lantern. In 2027, he returns to DC Comics in Deathstroke: The Terminator.
characters.signature: Weapon constructs — a soldier's arsenal forged from willpower.
characters.sources: Geoff Johns, Dave Gibbons (writers), Patrick Gleason (artist)

characters.name: Kryb
characters.tagline: The child-stealer — the Sinestro Corps' most terrifying predator.
characters.bio: Kryb is a hunchbacked alien of the Sinestro Corps with a ghoulish modus operandi: she hunts Green Lanterns who have newborn children. She murders the parents and steals the infants, keeping them in a cage-like growth on her back — a twisted 'family' of Green Lantern orphans. Her design by Ethan Van Sciver is among the most disturbing in the Corps: a gaunt, long-haired predator whose back bulges with stolen children. She was first introduced in a tale told by the captive Lyssa Drak, warning two expectant Green Lantern parents that Kryb would come for their child. She remains one of the Sinestro Corps' most feared members.
characters.signature: A back full of stolen children — fear given its cruelest form.

characters.name: Jo Mullein
characters.tagline: The Far Sector Lantern — Hugo Award-winning modern hero.
characters.bio: Sojourner 'Jo' Mullein is a former Earth police officer recruited by the Guardians for a top-secret mission to the Far Sector — a region so distant its numbering is uncertain. She was given a prototype ring that never needs recharging, designed to keep her off the grid as the Guardians' ace in the hole. Her series Far Sector (2019-2020), by novelist N.K. Jemisin and artist Jamal Campbell, won the 2022 Hugo Award for Best Graphic Story — the first Green Lantern story to win comics' most prestigious literary prize. Jo returned to a broken Corps after the Central Battery's destruction, rallying the survivors with the same determination that made her a great cop.
characters.signature: A self-sustaining ring — the Corps' secret weapon, no battery required.

characters.name: Jade
characters.tagline: Alan Scott's daughter — Earth's first female Green Lantern.
characters.bio: Jennifer-Lynn Hayden, known as Jade, is the daughter of Alan Scott — the Golden Age Green Lantern — and the villain Thorn. She inherited her father's Starheart powers, channeling green energy through the star-shaped birthmark on her palm rather than a ring. When Kyle Rayner gave her a spare power ring, she became Earth's first female Green Lantern and joined the Corps. Jade has served with the Justice Society, Infinity Inc., and the Justice League, carrying her father's legacy into the modern era.
characters.signature: Starheart energy through her palm — inherited power, no ring required.

characters.name: Green Man
characters.tagline: The Lantern of Uxor — a world without names.
characters.bio: Green Man hails from Uxor, a planet where inhabitants are not given proper names — he is known only by his title. Assigned to Sector 2828, which contains the Vega system, he served as the Green Lantern of a region the Guardians had pacted to avoid. He later partnered with Stel, the robotic Lantern of Grenda, and served with distinction through multiple Corps crises. His alien perspective — from a world without individual identity — gave him a unique understanding of the Corps' collective purpose.
characters.signature: A nameless Lantern — identity through service, not self.

characters.name: Jack T. Chance
characters.tagline: The Lantern of Hellhole — who brings a gun to a ring fight.
characters.bio: Jack T. Chance is the Green Lantern of Garnet, a world so crime-ridden it's called Hellhole. When the previous Lantern died, the ring chose Jack — a brutal enforcer who saw the ring as just another weapon. The Guardians were horrified by his methods but had no alternative; no one else would take the post. Jack was famously granted the sole exemption to the Corps' prohibition on lethal force, and he carried a pistol alongside his ring. He died fighting Parallax during Emerald Twilight, refusing to stand down.
characters.signature: A pistol and a power ring — the Corps' most controversial Lantern.

characters.name: Bzzd
characters.tagline: The wasp who fought like a giant.
characters.bio: Bzzd was a wasp-like Green Lantern from the planet Apiaton, assigned to Sector 2261 as the partner of Mogo — a pairing of the Corps' smallest and largest members. Constantly underestimated because of his size, Bzzd compensated with oversized constructs and unshakable willpower; his greatest fear was being stripped of his ring and returned to an insignificant insect. During the Sinestro Corps War he gave his life fighting Mongul to defend his fellow Lanterns, and his ring passed to Mother Mercy. He later rose as a Black Lantern, because even death could not keep so stubborn a will down for long.
characters.signature: Oversized constructs from the Corps' tiniest Lantern.

characters.name: Hannu
characters.tagline: The Lantern who fights with his fists, not his ring.
characters.bio: Hannu hails from Ovacron 6, where warriors consider weapons dishonorable — so this ten-foot, stone-skinned Lantern refuses to use his power ring in combat, employing it only for flight and transport. He fights with his bare hands, and his pride in his strength is matched only by his devotion to the Corps. Hannu was among the Lanterns sent to stop Hal Jordan during Emerald Twilight; defeated and stripped of his ring, he was left for dead, then captured by the Manhunters and imprisoned on Biot for years. He survived it all — one of the storied 'Lost Lanterns' — and returned to the Corps with his fists still his weapon of choice.
characters.signature: A ring worn as decoration — his fists do the talking.

characters.name: Voz
characters.tagline: Warden of the Sciencells — the Corps' most feared jailer.
characters.bio: Voz of Eciram, Sector 571, is one of the oldest and fiercest members of the Green Lantern Corps — a seven-foot, 816-pound wall of brown fur, claws, and absolute authority. After escaping the Draal, an alien species that cloned Lanterns and stole their rings, Voz's fearlessness convinced the Guardians to appoint him warden of the Sciencells, the most impenetrable prison in the cosmos. No inmate has ever been rehabilitated on his watch, and none has ever escaped — until the Red Lantern Vice broke free during the Emerald Eclipse and overpowered even Voz. He takes the failure personally, because for Voz, the Sciencells are not a posting. They are a sacred trust.
characters.signature: Ring and claws — the law of the Sciencells.

characters.name: Tomar-Tu
characters.tagline: The son who inherited his hero's ring — and his name.
characters.bio: Tomar-Tu is a Xudarian Green Lantern of Sector 2813 and the son of the legendary Tomar-Re — though he didn't know it at first. Born on the Mosaic World, a patchwork planet assembled by the mad Guardian Appa Ali Apsa from stolen cities, Tomar-Tu grew up idolizing Tomar-Re as a hero before discovering the hero was his father. He earned his own ring in Green Lantern vol. 3 #24 (1992) and served with distinction, counting as one of the Lost Lanterns who survived Parallax's rampage. Carrying the Tomar name means carrying its legacy — and Tomar-Tu has spent his career proving he deserves both.
characters.signature: A legacy Lantern — earning a name he was born to.

characters.name: Ash
characters.bio: Ashel Sabian Formanta — known as Ash — is the Green Lantern of Sector 650, a former farmer from the planet Arata whose wife Tasha was killed by vampires. He turned his grief into a crusade, hunting the blood-drinkers across his sector with his ring. Ash survived the fall of the Corps during Emerald Twilight and rejoined when it was rebuilt. His defining mission came during the War of Light, when the scarred Guardian sent him into the lightless Sector 666 to find the Anti-Monitor's corpse. There he met Saarek, and together they found the Black Central Power Battery on Ryut — and their deaths. Both rose as Black Lanterns when the dead rose.
characters.signature: A farmer turned hunter — fearless in the dark.

characters.name: Saarek
characters.tagline: The Lantern who speaks with the dead.
characters.bio: Saarek is the Green Lantern of Sector 773, a telepath from the planet Vulcan who claims he can commune with the dead — a claim most of the Corps met with skepticism. His gift proved real and terrible: he identified the killers who were harvesting the eyes of Lanterns' families by reading the last image in a victim's eye. The scarred Guardian chose him for a secret mission into Sector 666 to find the Anti-Monitor's corpse, where he met Ash. Together they discovered the Black Central Power Battery on Ryut, and the countless dead screaming in Saarek's mind overwhelmed him. He died there — and rose as a Black Lantern, the dead he once spoke to now his masters.
characters.signature: He heard the dead — until he joined them.

characters.name: G'nort
characters.bio: G'nort is a dog-like humanoid alien and, by every measure the Guardians use, the least qualified being ever to wear a power ring — which is exactly why fans adore him. He debuted in Justice League International #10 (1988), bumbling into the League during the Millennium crossover, and briefly served as the team's Green Lantern before being kicked out. The truth was stranger than the comedy: his ring was a fake, planted by the Weaponers of Qward through the clown-like Poglachians to discredit the Corps. But when it mattered, on Qward itself, G'nort saved Guy Gardner's life and destroyed the source of the fake rings — earning a genuine ring and the reluctant respect of the real Guardians. He lost it all in Emerald Twilight, served with the Darkstars, and was later revealed as Larfleeze's cousin. Useless? Often. Fearless? Always.
characters.signature: Earned a real ring on Qward by saving Guy Gardner.

characters.name: Graf Toren
characters.tagline: The Light Monk who hunted the Spider Guild.
characters.bio: Graf Toren was a Karaxian Light Monk who spent years hunting the Spider Guild across his sector before the Guardians chose him as their Lantern. He debuted in Guy Gardner #11 (August 1993), created by Chuck Dixon and Joe Staton, and his hexagonal, orange-skinned design made him one of the most visually distinctive Lanterns of the era. Toren stood among the Lanterns who tried to stop Hal Jordan's rampage on Oa during Emerald Twilight — and fell. But death was not the end: he was discovered years later in suspended animation on Biot, the Manhunter homeworld, where the Cyborg Superman had been using forgotten Lanterns as living power sources. Freed by Hal Jordan and Guy Gardner, Toren became one of the Lost Lanterns and fought through the Sinestro Corps War, finally getting the second chance his first death denied him.
characters.signature: A monk's discipline behind a warrior's ring.

characters.name: Charlie Vicker
characters.tagline: The actor who became the real thing.
characters.bio: Charlie Vicker was a flamboyant television actor famous for playing Green Lantern on an Earth TV show — until life imitated art in the worst way. When space criminals mistook his stand-in brother Roger for the real Lantern during a live broadcast, Roger was killed, and a guilt-stricken Charlie demanded Hal Jordan take him along to hunt the murderer. Hal deputized him with a fallen Lantern's ring in Green Lantern (vol. 2) #55 (September 1967), and Charlie proved himself so thoroughly that the Guardians granted him a ring of his own and assigned him to Sector 3319. After the Corps fell he joined John Stewart's Darkstars, died in the Battle of Rann, and — like so many Lanterns — returned when the Corps was reborn, answering the call again during the War of the Green Lanterns. He began as a man pretending to be a hero, and became one for real.
characters.signature: From TV hero to true Lantern of Sector 3319.
